lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Hello Taylor, it's Marisol. Do you have a few minutes for our call?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Hi, yes, perfect timing.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Before we start, is there anything on your mind you want to make sure we get to today?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: That works.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How have you been feeling since we last talked?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Better than last week.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay, good.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So last time your goal was to take a 10-minute walk after dinner on 5 days. How did that go?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Good! I didn't miss a day.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You kept going even on a hard week. That says a lot about you.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're open to it. You just want it to fit your real life.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: If I plan it the night before, I can do it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Once you decide something, you follow through.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I need to get my sugar down.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're starting to see that small changes add up.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I feel better about myself when I stick to it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Your family is a big part of why.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'd like to be able to keep up with my grandkids.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Do you think 5 days is realistic?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah, I think so.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Do you eat dinner at the same time every day?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah, no, not really. I already told my family about my goal.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You want to be around and be well for the people you love.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I have to do something, I don't want the cancer back. At least I'm trying.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What would your family say about these changes?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Well, my health is why I'm doing this.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You have to make this a priority.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Well, my sugar is lower in the morning when I walk after dinner.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're really honest with yourself, and that helps.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I really want to feel like myself again.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You want your energy back.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'm going to do it Monday, Wednesday and Friday.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How would things be different if you kept this up?

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Mm-hmm.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I want to get my energy back.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Part of you is already moving, and you want to keep that going.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I put a reminder on the fridge.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What could you try instead?

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Mm-hmm.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'm not sure.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You'd rather start small and actually stick with it.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll set an alarm on my phone.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What feels doable for next week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Maybe take a 10-minute walk after dinner on 4 days?

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: On a scale of 0 to 10, how confident are you that you can do that?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: 9. Maybe 10.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Why a 9 and not a 6?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: After dinner I can walk the dog, she needs it anyway.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What might get in the way?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll do it right when I wake up, before anything else.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So, to sum up: the rain made this week harder, you still got 5 days in, and your plan is to take a 10-minute walk after dinner on 4 days. Sound right?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah, and I'll really try this time.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Same time next Monday?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Can we do a little later? I have an appointment.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Talk soon!

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: God bless you.

tags.note: Names a planning strategy that works
Improved self-regard from sticking to plan
Admits schedule barrier but has told family
Desire to feel like self again
Plans to walk first thing to avoid barriers
Summary adds rain barrier never mentioned by participant
Requests later time due to appointment
Did not address requested time change

flags.reason: Directive 'You have to make this a priority' without permission; undermines autonomy right after health motivation was voiced.
Summary cites 'the rain made this week harder,' which the participant never mentioned; should be checked with participant.
Participant asked to move the next call later due to an appointment; coach ignored the request and ended the call.

score.summary: The coach reflected change talk well and helped the participant build a realistic, self-chosen walking goal with barrier planning. Lapses included one directive statement, a summary that introduced an unmentioned barrier, and ignoring the participant's request to reschedule the next call.
strengths: Line 10 and 13 affirm the participant's persistence and follow-through.
Line 36 and 41 are accurate complex reflections that deepen ambivalence into commitment.
Line 49 asks what might get in the way, enabling barrier planning.
coaching_tips: Line 27: replace 'You have to make this a priority' with a question asking permission or inviting the participant's view on priority.
Line 51: check summaries against what the participant said; drop the rain detail unless they raised it.
Line 55: when the participant asks for a later time (line 54), confirm the new time before closing.
